FOREWORD

OS TKIS Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 8 July 196% after the draft finalized by the Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 0.2 Drawing pins are used for holding the paper in position on the This standard deals with commonly used types of drawing boards. drawing pins in drawing offices. 0.3 In the preparation of this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from B.S. 1677:1959 " Draughtsmen's drawing pins" issued by the British Standards Institution. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final wdue, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shali be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2-1 960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified vahse in thh standard. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements fastening paper on drawing boards. 2. TYPES 2.1 The drawing pins shall be of the following types: a) Type A -- drawing pin with, domed or bevelled head, the pin `being screwed into the head or gripped by swaging or pinning; h) Type B -- drawing pin to be punched out of sheet in a circular shape, with three projections punched out and bent to shape; and c) Type C -- drawing pin punched out of sheet in the form of a three pointed star, the points being bent to shape. --.

7.1 All surfaces of the drawing pins shall be finished smooth. drawing pins shall be plated for resistance to corrosion. 8. PACKING AND MARKING

8.1 The drawing pins shall be packed in a cardboard carton of suitable size. The carton shall be marked with the type and size of the drawing pins and the number of drawing pins packed in the carton. 8.1.1 The carton containing IS1 Certification Mark. drawing pins may also be marked with the

NOTE - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act, and the Rules and Regulations Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indian Standard made thereunder. conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard, under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control during production. This system, which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer, has the further safeguard that the products as actually marketed are continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to the standard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.
